deepseek_columns.ai_commands: -- Delete LDAP  Config (`openbmctool.py ${BMC_CONN:?operator must supply openbmctool target, e.g. http://${BMC_USER}:${BMC_PASS}@${BMC_IP}:8080/} ldap disable`): disables LDAP on the BMC. Agent runs the tool and confirms HTTP 200; note root user must be enabled before disabling LDAP.
deepseek_columns.ai_logs_output: return the ldap disable output + HTTP 200 so the user confirms the LDAP config was removed.
deepseek_columns.risk: RISK: disabling LDAP removes an auth path; confirm admin access remains after.

historical_reviews.deepseek: PARTIAL recognizes an auth-path removal risk but places credentials in a URL-shaped connection example, assumes root must be enabled, equates HTTP 200 with removal and does not distinguish disabling LDAP from deleting its configuration, mappings or CA trust.
historical_reviews.gpt_v2: REQUIRES PACKAGE / USER CONFIRMATION / CHANGED correctly requires a pinned method, complete auth/account/session baseline, independently verified local recovery, one disable, full policy readback, LDAP denial, local-admin verification and no blind root enablement.
historical_reviews.round_02: Entry 928/2291 repeats the tool/status path and generic write gate without resolving delete-versus-disable semantics, proving access continuity or examining retained config, sessions and audit state.
historical_reviews.related_source_cases: The preceding Create rows establish non-secure or secure LDAP state; following privilege-mapping rows manipulate mappings. This row must state whether those objects and CA trust persist after `ldap disable` rather than assuming deletion.
historical_reviews.invalid_checkpoint_1000: No sequence-1090, Wistron-BMC-00219-V002 or e667fde9ca47b711 draft exists in the invalidated run.
historical_reviews.v3: No V3 overlay exists for this exact case.
historical_reviews.v3_1: ED-33 preserves the original openbmctool disable action unless an approved override records differences; ED-34 treats account/session/restore details as readiness inputs; ED-35 requires state and auth evidence beyond HTTP 200; ED-38 prohibits blind account enablement, retries and verdict claims.

original_test_intent: Verify the openbmctool LDAP disable operation removes the intended external authentication path while preserving a verified local administrator path, and determine whether the platform disables a retained LDAP object or actually deletes configuration as the title states.
original_method: Preserve the complete redacted LDAP/auth/account/session/CA/mapping state and independent recovery; pin the supported openbmctool version; verify a usable existing local admin without changing accounts; execute `ldap disable` once after approval; capture response and audit evidence; read back enabled state and retained/removed properties; reject new LDAP authentication, verify local access and session behavior; restore only through a separate approved action.
manual_activity: An owner decides whether acceptance is disabled external authentication with retained settings or deletion of the LDAP object and related artifacts. A human verifies an already-enabled local recovery account and independent console before approval, observes access/session behavior and controls any restore. Automation may issue one pinned disable and collect redacted readback, but may not enable root or decide the verdict.
required_inputs: BMC/firmware identity and pinned supported openbmctool/API version
Verified enabled local-admin account and independent console/recovery path
Expected disable-versus-delete state for URI, CA, mappings and sessions
Allowed LDAP-denial and local-login/role/session acceptance matrix
Approved restore/recreate payload and recovery method
Engineer disposition of the title/procedure semantic difference
safety_requirements: Do not blindly enable root, bulk-enable local users or change protected account state merely to satisfy the note; use an approved already-verified recovery account or separately govern the account change.
Do not place BMC credentials in URLs, command lines, history, process listings, screenshots, logs or review JSON, and do not clear security/audit evidence.
Stop before disable if LDAP is the only verified admin path, the target is uncertain, active security work conflicts or no independent console exists.
Obtain point-of-action approval for one disable. Do not retry on timeout, terminate unrelated sessions or restore/recreate LDAP without separate approval.
Do not treat HTTP 200 as deletion. Independently read the enabled state, retained object/CA/mappings, new-login behavior, local access and audit event.
Stop on local login failure, unexpected session/role changes, partial state, continued new LDAP access or lost recovery; preserve evidence and use the approved console recovery.
agent_execution_scope: Validate target, pinned tool, complete auth/LDAP/CA/mapping/account/session baseline, existing local recovery, expected semantics and restore plan; present the exact disable for approval.
After approval, run one protected `ldap disable`, capture redacted response/audit and read back both enablement and retained/removed properties.
Verify rejection of a new approved LDAP login, continued independent local-admin access, roles and defined existing-session behavior.
Archive evidence and stop without root enablement, deletion assumption, automatic retry, unapproved restore or DUT verdict.
engineer_actions: Resolve whether `Delete LDAP Config` means only disablement or deletion of the LDAP object, CA trust and privilege mappings, and define session behavior.
Approve the pinned disable, existing recovery account, acceptance matrix and any later restore/recreate action.
Review state/auth/session/audit and recovery evidence and issue the formal verdict.

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: The `ldap disable` operation fits the Procedure but not necessarily the title's delete semantics. DeepSeek's connection example can expose credentials, HTTP 200 proves only request handling, and its statement that config was removed is unsupported without property readback.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Use the exact pinned vendor openbmctool `ldap disable` action once with protected authentication, then separately read enabled state, retained LDAP/CA/mapping properties, auth behavior, sessions and audit events.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: The openbmctool disable command, Delete title, 200 Criteria, root/local-user warning and cited phosphor-user-manager reference, no Script and 10/0-minute estimates remain preserved; Review does not silently convert disable into delete.

modernized_recommendation.status: PROJECT EXECUTION READINESS PENDING; ENGINEER DECISION PENDING FOR DELETE VERSUS DISABLE
modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Perform one recovery-gated disable, then prove external-auth denial, local recovery and exact persistence/removal of configuration, mappings, CA and sessions before any separately approved restore.
modernized_recommendation.applicable_platform: The selected OpenBMC LDAP/user-manager implementation and its supported openbmctool disable action.
modernized_recommendation.supported_version: Record BMC firmware/API, openbmctool commit/runtime and user-manager revision.
modernized_recommendation.official_reference: Pinned openbmc-tools/phosphor-user-manager behavior, vendor auth schema, Project access-control policy and recovery SOP.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds recovery, protected credentials, exact state semantics and real authentication/session verification while retaining the source disable and title conflict.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: A vendor API override does not prove openbmctool; disabled-but-retained configuration is not deletion; local login does not alone prove LDAP rejection or session policy.
modernized_recommendation.required_inputs: Baseline, recovery account, expected persistence/deletion, session/auth matrix and restore plan.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Disabling LDAP can strand users; enabling root adds a separate credential risk; retained mappings/CA can influence later re-enable behavior.

project_override_considerations: A Project may use a supported vendor API or WebUI only when it records the original openbmctool disable, actual method, reason, engineer approval, equivalent state/auth/session coverage and unverified tool behavior. It may not claim object deletion unless readback proves the specified artifacts are removed.
expected_evidence: Approved target/change, BMC/firmware, pinned tool, redacted full LDAP/auth/CA/mapping/account/session baseline and independent local-recovery proof
One protected disable response and security audit event with no credential exposure or log clearing
Post-readback showing LDAP enabled state and exact retained/removed URI, directory fields, CA and privilege mappings
New LDAP-login denial, successful local-admin login/role and expected existing-session behavior from independent observers
No root/bulk-account change or retry, known restore state, delete-versus-disable engineer disposition and engineer-owned verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Items say `Delete LDAP Config`, while the sole Procedure command is `ldap disable`; neither Criteria nor notes establish whether the configuration object, CA trust or mappings are deleted. Disabled retained state and deletion are materially different operations and recovery states. Master remains preserved and an engineer must define authoritative semantics.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The external-auth disable and access-continuity purpose is identifiable, and post-readback can expose platform behavior. The delete-versus-disable ambiguity remains engineer-owned but does not require a permanent BLOCKED classification for review or readiness planning.

comparison_to_prior_reviews.deepseek: Keeps PACKAGE but rejects credential-bearing shorthand and HTTP-only proof, adds state/auth/session/recovery evidence and stops claiming removal without readback.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.gpt_v2: Agrees with its lockout safeguards and explicitly elevates title Delete versus command Disable to a source conflict rather than merging the meanings.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.round_02: Replaces a generic write gate with exact persistence, LDAP denial, local access, session and audit checkpoints.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.related_source_cases: Preserves Create and privilege-mapping coverage separately and checks whether their artifacts persist instead of assuming this row deletes them.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.invalid_checkpoint_1000: No invalid draft exists for this exact source identity.

review_improvement: Prevents an HTTP response from being misreported as configuration deletion and protects management access by verifying local recovery before changing the external-auth path.
independent_technical_reasoning: An enable flag can turn off LDAP authentication while retaining URI, CA and role mappings for later re-enable; that is not equivalent to deleting configuration. The source names one behavior and commands the other. The safe evidence model must observe both state and authentication from independent sessions, because HTTP success can coexist with continued LDAP access, a partial change or local lockout.
